The test image shows a tomato fruit (red/orange surface) with numerous dark, spiky/hairy fungal structures scattered across it — these appear to be black sporangia on stalks, with white mycelium visible in the center. This strongly suggests Rhizopus Soft Rot.

Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The reference image shows a later-stage collapsed fruit, while the test image shows an earlier close-up view of the characteristic fungal structures. The test image features:

- **Red/orange tomato fruit surface** (pod)
- **Numerous black sporangia on stalks** with radiating spines — classic Rhizopus sporangiophores
- **White mycelium** in the center area
- Slight water-soaking/sunken appearance of the fruit surface

This perfectly matches the Rhizopus Soft Rots description: "whitish-gray mycelia with black sporangia." The spiky black balls on stalks scattered across the fruit surface are diagnostic for *Rhizopus stolonifer*.
